title: The day before the Constitution was adopted, its own architect warned the country not to trust it blindly. November 25, 2026.
excerpt: Ambedkar's closing speech to the Constituent Assembly, a Kerala schoolboy's global education award, India's new lithium and nickel processing push, and the journalist who built a 96%-recovery waste business.
bodyHtml:
The day before the Constitution was adopted, its own architect warned the country not to trust it blindly

On November 25, 1949, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar delivered his closing speech to the Constituent Assembly, a day before the Constitution was formally adopted. He warned that a good constitution alone couldn't guarantee good governance - if things went wrong, he said, it wouldn't be because the Constitution was bad, but because the people entrusted to run it failed to live up to it.

He was sent back to Kerala at age 4 for school. He just won a global award named after a US President

Sunny Varkey won the 2026 Eisenhower Global Transformation Award at a New York gala on November 9, 2026. Born in Ranni, Kerala, Varkey's family moved to Dubai when he was very young, but he was sent back to Kerala around age 4 for schooling. He went on to found GEMS Education, the world's largest private K-12 school operator, and the Varkey Foundation's Global Teacher Prize.

India just approved funding to build its own lithium and nickel processing plants

The Union Cabinet approved a Rs 2,814 crore scheme to build domestic lithium and nickel processing plants over five years, funding four new plants with the government covering 30% of the capital cost through competitive bidding - a push to cut India's reliance on imported refined critical minerals.

A former journalist turned Bengaluru's trash problem into a business that recovers 96% of what it handles

Wilma Rodrigues, a former Mumbai journalist, moved to Bengaluru in 2000 and started Saahas in 2001 to help implement India's first municipal solid waste rules. In 2013, she spun that work into Saahas Zero Waste, a for-profit circular-economy business that recovered over 96% of the waste it handled last financial year.

Four stories today, one thread: people and institutions that built something to last longer than the moment that created them.
